copy.home.about.heading: More about me
copy.home.about.p1: I film events and make short films about movement, and I edit everything myself.
copy.home.about.p2: I film events because the best moments are never on the schedule. I film circus and dance because I perform and teach it, so I know when to move closer and when to stay out of the way.
copy.home.about.p3: I often work with Slipstream Circus Collective, the Portland circus and digital arts collective I founded.
copy.home.about.loc: Portland, Oregon. Vimeo and Instagram links go here.
copy.form.title: Tell me about your project
copy.form.intro: Share the kind of film, what it is for, and when.
copy.form.book_prompt: Prefer to talk it through first?
copy.form.label_msg: What do you have in mind?
copy.events.hero.title: Event videography in Portland, Oregon
copy.events.hero.lede: I film galas, conferences, concerts, and celebrations around Portland, then edit the day into a film you can share. The aim is a film people want to watch twice: the speeches that mattered, the room, and the moments nobody scheduled.
copy.events.what.heading: What I film
copy.events.what.1.title: Galas and fundraisers.
copy.events.what.1.body: The room, the speeches, and the people who make the night work.
copy.events.what.2.title: Conferences and talks.
copy.events.what.2.body: Speakers, panels, and the conversations in the hallway.
copy.events.what.3.title: Concerts and live performances.
copy.events.what.3.body: The stage, the crowd, and the moments between songs.
copy.events.what.4.title: Celebrations.
copy.events.what.4.body: Parties, openings, and anniversaries worth keeping.
copy.events.how.heading: How it works
copy.events.how.1.title: First, we talk.
copy.events.how.1.body: Tell me the date, the place, and what the film is for. We decide what has to be captured and what is a bonus.
copy.events.how.2.title: Then I plan the coverage.
copy.events.how.2.body: I ask about the schedule, any speeches or performances, and the venue, and I arrive early to set up.
copy.events.how.3.title: On the day, I stay out of the way.
copy.events.how.3.body: I film from the edges, avoid interrupting, and work alongside your staff and any photographers.
copy.events.how.4.title: Afterward, I edit.
copy.events.how.4.body: You get a highlight film you can share, and longer cuts of speeches or performances if you ask for them.
copy.events.deliverables.heading: What you can ask for
copy.events.deliverables.body: A highlight film for sharing. Full-length cuts of speeches, talks, or performances. Short versions for social media. If you need something else, ask.
copy.events.portland.heading: Filming in Portland
copy.events.portland.body: Filming indoors at a private venue is usually settled between you, the venue, and me. Filming on streets, sidewalks, or in city parks is different. The City of Portland's Events and Film Office is the place to start for permits, and street and sidewalk permits ask for at least three business days' notice and proof of insurance. Many venues also ask vendors for a certificate of insurance. If your plans involve any of this, tell me early and we will sort it out together.
copy.events.faq.heading: Questions
copy.events.faq.1.q: How far ahead should I book?
copy.events.faq.1.a: As early as you can. Dates fill, especially in event season, so write as soon as you have one.
copy.events.faq.2.a: It depends on how long the event runs, how many places I need to be, and what you want back. Tell me about your day and I will send a quote.
copy.events.faq.3.a: We agree this in writing before the event: what you can use the film for, and what I can show in my own portfolio.
copy.events.faq.4.a: Mostly in and around Portland. If your event is further away, ask.
copy.dance.hero.title: Dance, circus, and performance films in Portland
copy.dance.hero.lede: I make short films with dancers, jugglers, and circus artists: studio pieces, work made for a particular place, and clear documentation of a live show. I am a circus artist and teacher myself, so I know how a routine is built and where the camera should and should not be.
copy.dance.what.heading: What I make
copy.dance.what.1.title: Short films.
copy.dance.what.1.body: Made for the screen, usually built together with the artist, in a studio or in a place that suits the work.
copy.dance.what.2.title: Show documentation.
copy.dance.what.2.body: A live performance filmed clearly, so it can be watched, shared, and submitted.
copy.dance.what.3.title: Reels for artists.
copy.dance.what.3.body: A tight reel for auditions, festivals, venues, and funders.
copy.dance.what.4.title: Collaborations.
copy.dance.what.4.body: Work that grows from an idea, whether it starts with you or with me.
copy.dance.how.heading: How it works
copy.dance.how.1.title: We start with the act or the idea.
copy.dance.how.1.body: What are you making, who is it for, and where will it be seen?
copy.dance.how.2.title: I plan the film around the performer.
copy.dance.how.2.body: Location, light, and what the camera should see, decided together before anyone picks up a camera.
copy.dance.how.3.title: I film with you, not around you.
copy.dance.how.3.body: I am a circus artist, juggler, and teacher myself, so I know how a routine is built and when to move closer or stay back.
copy.dance.how.4.title: Then I edit.
copy.dance.how.4.body: We watch it together and refine it until it is right.
copy.dance.funding.heading: Funding and submissions
copy.dance.funding.body: A good film is often part of a grant or festival application. Tell me what you are applying to and the format they ask for, and I will cut to it.
copy.dance.origin.heading: Where I come from
copy.dance.origin.body: I perform and teach in Portland, and I often work with Slipstream Circus Collective, the Portland circus and digital arts collective I founded.
copy.dance.portland.heading: Filming in Portland
copy.dance.portland.body: Filming in a studio is simple. Filming on streets, sidewalks, or in city parks is different. The City of Portland's Events and Film Office is the place to start for permits, and street and sidewalk permits ask for at least three business days' notice and proof of insurance. Many venues also ask vendors for a certificate of insurance. If your plans involve any of this, tell me early and we will sort it out together.
copy.dance.faq.heading: Questions
copy.dance.faq.1.a: Yes. I can document a performance so it can be watched afterward, and I will agree the camera positions with you first so I do not get in anyone's way.
copy.dance.faq.2.q: What if I have never made a film?
copy.dance.faq.2.a: That is fine. We start from what you want to show, and I will guide the rest.
copy.dance.faq.3.a: It depends on the length of the piece, the filming days, and the editing. Tell me about the project and I will send a quote.
copy.editing.hero.title: Video editing in Portland, Oregon
copy.editing.hero.lede: Bring me footage you have shot and I will shape it into a finished film, a teaser, or a reel. I edit events, performances, and promotional videos, and I care about rhythm, sound, and what to leave out.
copy.editing.what.heading: What I edit
copy.editing.what.1.title: Event films.
copy.editing.what.1.body: Raw coverage shaped into a highlight film or a set of longer cuts.
copy.editing.what.2.title: Performance and dance films.
copy.editing.what.2.body: Work made for the screen, or a live show cut so it is worth watching.
copy.editing.what.3.title: Teasers and trailers.
copy.editing.what.3.body: Short, sharp pieces to announce a show or an event.
copy.editing.what.4.title: Showreels.
copy.editing.what.4.body: A reel for a performer, a company, or a videographer.
copy.editing.how.heading: How it works
copy.editing.how.1.title: Send the footage.
copy.editing.how.1.body: A link to a shared folder is enough. Tell me what the film is for, how long it should run, and where it will be seen.
copy.editing.how.2.title: We agree the rounds.
copy.editing.how.2.body: Before I start, we settle how many rounds of feedback are included, so there are no surprises.
copy.editing.how.3.title: I send a first cut.
copy.editing.how.3.body: You tell me what works and what does not, and I refine it.
copy.editing.how.4.title: Then I finish it.
copy.editing.how.4.body: Sound, color, titles, and the files you need for every place the film will live.
copy.editing.music.heading: Music and rights
copy.editing.music.body: Music has to be licensed for the way the film will be used. If you already have music, tell me where it comes from. If you do not, I can work with licensed tracks.
copy.editing.remote.heading: Remote or in person
copy.editing.remote.body: Most editing happens remotely, with footage arriving by link. If you are in Portland and would rather review a cut together, we can meet.
copy.editing.faq.heading: Questions
copy.editing.faq.1.q: What footage can you work with?
copy.editing.faq.1.a: Most professional and consumer cameras. Tell me what you shot on and roughly how much there is.
copy.editing.faq.2.a: It depends on the length and complexity of the film. Tell me your deadline when you write, and I will say plainly whether it works.
copy.editing.faq.3.a: I quote by the project, once I know how much footage there is and what you want to end up with.
